home.q: Why is my sliding glass door so hard to open?
home.a: Usually it's sand or grit in the track, rollers that are worn or seized, or a panel that has dropped out of level and drags on the sill. Vacuum the track first. If it still takes two hands, the rollers need adjusting or replacing.

home.q: Is it worth repairing a sliding glass door or should I replace it?
home.a: Repair it if the frame is straight and solid. Rollers, tracks, locks and weatherstrip are replaceable parts. Replacement makes sense when the frame is corroded or bent, the glass needs an impact upgrade, or repairs keep piling up.

home.q: How much does sliding glass door repair cost?
home.a: It depends on the part and the door. A roller adjustment is quick work, while new rollers, a track cap or a glass unit cost more in parts and time. Impact glass, oversized panels and hard-to-find hardware raise the price. We quote after seeing the door or a photo.

home.q: Why is there fog between the panes of my sliding door?
home.a: The seal around the insulated glass unit has failed, and the drying agent inside is saturated with moisture. You can't wipe it away from either side. The glass unit needs replacing, so check whether the door's glass warranty still covers it.

home.q: Why does water come in under my sliding glass door when it rains?
home.a: Most often the weep holes that drain the sill are clogged, so water rises over the inside lip. Worn weatherstrip and a panel set too high also let water past. In a hurricane, wind can push rain through even a well-kept sill.

home.q: Does salt air damage sliding glass doors?
home.a: Yes. Salt holds moisture against metal rollers, screws and aluminum tracks, which speeds up corrosion. Near the coast, plan to clean and inspect doors every three months instead of every six.

home.q: What should I check on my sliding doors before hurricane season?
home.a: Clear the weep holes, confirm the lock engages fully, and look for cracked glass or a sagging panel. Season starts June 1, so April or May gives time to order parts. Shutters or impact glass are a separate question for your door's product approval.

home.q: Is it safe to keep using a sliding door with cracked glass?
home.a: Not for long. A crack weakens the pane, and a tempered pane can shatter all at once. Keep children and pets clear, tape it as a short-term measure, and get a safety-glass replacement made to size.

home.q: Can I fix a sliding glass door myself?
home.a: Some of it. Cleaning the track, clearing weep holes and small roller height adjustments are reasonable DIY jobs. Lifting a glass panel out of the frame takes two people, and glass replacement should be left to someone with the right equipment.

home.q: Why won't my sliding door close all the way?
home.a: Check the track for debris first, then the gap around the panel. A panel that has dropped at one end hits the jamb at an angle and stops short. A bent track or a loose interlock strip can do the same.

home.q: Which parts of Florida do you serve?
home.a: Our crews work across Florida. We're based in South Florida, and the cities listed on this page and in the footer are some of the places we serve. If your town isn't listed, call us and we'll tell you when a crew can get there.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: Can I replace sliding glass door rollers myself?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: Often, yes, if you have a helper and the right part. The glass panel usually has to be lifted out of the frame, and that's dangerous to do alone. Heavy impact panels are best left to a pro.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: How do I know if my sliding door rollers are bad?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: Raise the rollers first. If the door still drags or grinds, the wheels are likely cracked, worn flat or seized. Once the panel is out, spin each wheel by hand: rough spots, wobble or rust on the axle mean it's done.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: Which way do I turn the screw to raise my sliding door?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: It depends on the roller. Some rollers rise when turned clockwise and others drop. Lift the panel slightly, turn a quarter turn, and check whether the gap at the top got smaller or bigger.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: Where is the roller adjustment screw on a sliding glass door?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: At the two bottom corners of the moving panel, either on the inside face or on the vertical edge. Many doors hide the holes under small plastic caps that pry out with a flat screwdriver.

No. Rollers differ in wheel diameter, wheel width, edge shape, housing size, mounting style and where the adjustment screw sits. Measure the old one, or take it with you to a parts counter, before buying a replacement.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: What is the difference between single and tandem rollers?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: A single roller has one wheel in its housing. A tandem has two wheels in line, which spreads a heavy panel's weight over more contact points. Replace like with like, because the housing sizes differ.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: Are stainless steel rollers worth it near the beach?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: Usually, yes. Stainless resists salt corrosion far better than plated steel, which starts to rust once its coating wears through. The catch is fit: stainless has to be made in the exact size your panel takes.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: Can I replace just the wheel instead of the whole roller?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: Sometimes. A few roller assemblies take replacement wheels on their own, but many wheels are riveted into the housing. For those, and for any housing with rust or a stripped adjustment screw, replace the whole assembly.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: Do I have to take the door off to replace the rollers?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: On most doors, yes: the panel is lifted up and swung out at the bottom. Some aluminum doors allow a roller swap by removing the vertical side pieces of the panel instead, but that depends on how the door was built.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: Should I oil my sliding door rollers?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: Follow your door maker's care sheet, since makers disagree. Some call for light oil where the shaft passes through the wheel, while others use sealed bearings meant to run dry. Never pack the track with grease.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: How many rollers does a sliding glass door have?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: Two per moving panel, one at each bottom corner. A three or four panel door has rollers on every panel that slides. Fixed panels sit on the frame and don't roll.

sliding-door-roller-replacement.q: How much weight can sliding door rollers hold?
sliding-door-roller-replacement.a: It depends on the roller's rating. The industry roller standard tests roller assemblies at their rated load, with ratings running from 75 pounds to over 600 pounds. A heavy impact panel needs rollers rated for it.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: Can a sliding door track be repaired, or does it have to be replaced?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: Most tracks can be repaired. Dirt cleans out, small bends straighten, and a worn or grooved rail can get a stainless cap. Replacement is for a rail that's cracked, broken off, or a sill corroded along its length.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: Do sliding door track repair caps actually work?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: Yes, on a rail that's worn but still intact. The cap bonds over the old rail and gives the rollers a smooth stainless surface. It won't fix a broken rail, and it needs to match your rail's height and width.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: How do I know what size track cap I need?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: Measure the height and width of the raised rail your rollers ride on, in sixteenths of an inch. Compare that with the opening on the cap's package drawing. Prime-Line's stainless cap drawing, for example, shows a profile of 1/4 by 3/16 inch.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: How do I get sand out of a sliding door track?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: Vacuum both channels with a crevice tool, then blow out the corners with compressed air, which works best on sand and salt. Wipe with a damp cloth and let it dry before adding any lubricant.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: What lubricant should I use on a sliding door track?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: The one your door's maker names in its care guide. Some makers call for spray silicone wiped on with a cloth, while others say to avoid silicone and use a marine lubricant. Apply a thin film, never a heavy coat.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: Is WD-40 OK for a sliding door track?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: We'd skip it. We didn't find a door maker that recommends regular WD-40 for tracks, and oily residue holds sand. Clean the track and use the product named in your door's care sheet instead.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: What are the little slots in the bottom of my sliding door track for?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: They're weep slots, part of the door's drainage. Rainwater that gets into the sill collects in the channel and drains out through them to weep holes on the outside face of the sill.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: How do I unclog the weep holes on a sliding glass door?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: Pour a cup of water into the inside channel to find the blocked one. Then work a pipe cleaner or thin wire gently into the outside hole, or use compressed air. Don't push the wire deep, since it can damage the glass unit.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: Should I caulk my weep holes to stop leaks?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: No. Sealing a weep hole traps water inside the sill, where it overflows onto the floor or damages the wall below. If caulk is already there, cut and scrape it out, and look for the real source of the leak.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: What is the black residue on my aluminum sliding door track?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: It's oxidation from bare aluminum. It wipes off as a dark residue with a fine scratch pad. It's cosmetic until it turns into pitting on top of the rail, which wears roller wheels.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: Can I pressure wash my sliding door track?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: It's better not to. A pressure washer can force water into the sill faster than the weep holes drain it, and it can drive grit into places you can't reach. Use a vacuum, a brush and a damp cloth.

sliding-door-track-repair.q: What is a sill riser on a sliding door?
sliding-door-track-repair.a: It's the raised inner wall of the sill that holds back water blown in by wind. Inspectors after Hurricane Ian found some sliding doors lacked adequate sill risers, which let storm rain spill into homes.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: Why won't my sliding door lock line up anymore?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: Usually the panel has dropped. Worn or settled rollers lower the door, so the hook swings under the keeper instead of into it. Raise the panel with the roller screws, then slide the keeper up or down in its slotted holes.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: How do I adjust the latch on a sliding glass door?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: Close the door slowly and watch where the hook meets the keeper. Loosen the keeper's two screws, slide it to meet the hook, and tighten. Some mortise locks also have a screw on the faceplate that changes how far the hook reaches.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: How do I measure a sliding door handle for replacement?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: Measure the distance between the two mounting screw holes, center to center. Common sizes include 3-15/16, 4-15/16 and 6-5/8 inches. Also measure the panel thickness, since each handle set fits a limited range.

No. Handles vary in screw spacing, panel thickness range, and whether they work a separate mortise lock or have the hook built in. A handle that fits your holes can still fail to work your lock if the lever doesn't match.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: What is a mortise lock on a sliding door?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: It's the latch mechanism housed in a pocket cut into the edge of the sliding panel, held by two screws through a faceplate. The handle on the face only carries the lever that moves the hook in and out.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: Can I add a keyed lock to my sliding door?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: Often, yes. Some non-keyed handle sets accept a cylinder conversion kit, and others can be swapped for a keyed set with the same screw spacing. Check that the new set works with the lock body already in your door.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: Can a locked sliding glass door be lifted off its track?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: Many older ones can. A slider can be lifted up and out, defeating the latch. Anti-lift screws or blocks in the upper track and properly adjusted rollers prevent it.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: Is a security bar or a dowel in the track better?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: Both block the panel from sliding. A fold-down security bar mounts at mid-height, is easy to see from outside and swings out of the way when you need the door. A dowel works but is easy to forget and can be a trip hazard.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: Does a sliding door to the pool need an alarm in Florida?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: It's one of the options. For a new residential pool to pass final inspection, Florida law requires one of five safety features, and one is an 85 dB A exit alarm on doors with direct pool access. Ask your building department about your situation.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: Why is my sliding door handle loose?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: The through-screws holding the inside and outside halves together have backed out, or the screw holes in the panel have worn. Tighten them gently. If the handle still wobbles, the mounting bosses may be cracked and the set needs replacing.

sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.q: Should I replace the lock and handle at the same time?
sliding-door-lock-and-handle-repair.a: Not always. If only the handle is cracked and the lock body works, a matching handle is enough. When the lock is worn, replacing both together avoids mismatched levers and keyways, especially on older doors.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: Why does my sliding screen door keep falling off the track?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Usually the small spring rollers at the bottom are worn, cracked or adjusted too high, so the screen loses its grip between the top and bottom tracks. A bent screen frame or a dented outer rail causes the same thing.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: Is it worth rescreening a sliding screen door or should I buy a new one?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Rescreen it if the frame is straight and the corners are tight. Replace the screen door if the frame is bent, the corners have split, or the rails are chewed up from coming off the track.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: Are screen door rollers the same as sliding glass door rollers?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: No. Screen rollers are smaller, lighter spring-tension wheels made for a frame that weighs very little. Glass door rollers carry the full weight of the glass panel. Measure the old screen roller before buying a new one.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: Can I patch a hole in a screen door instead of replacing the screen?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: For a small, clean hole, yes. A patch kit keeps bugs out even if it shows. If the mesh is brittle and crumbles when pressed, it's sun-damaged all over, and a full rescreen is the only lasting fix.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: What size spline do I need for my screen door?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Match a piece of the old spline. Typical sizing is .140 inch for standard fiberglass in common grooves and .125 inch for aluminum mesh. Go one size smaller when switching to thicker pet or solar screen.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: Will no-see-um screen keep out no-see-ums completely?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Not completely. A 20 by 20 mesh stops far more than standard screen, but a University of Arizona extension sheet suggests 30 by 30 mesh where possible for biting midges. Expect fewer bites, not none.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: What's the difference between 18x16 and 18x14 screen?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: The numbers are strands per inch in each direction. 18 by 16 is the standard fiberglass mesh. 18 by 14 is a heavier pool and patio mesh with thicker strands, made for bigger openings.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: What is the best screen for a house near the beach?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Fiberglass-based mesh. Fiberglass, sun control screens and tougher pet-resistant meshes all suit coastal areas. Aluminum mesh doesn't, since salt air works on bare metal.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: Can I put solar screen on a sliding screen door?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Yes. Solar screen mesh is sold for door screens and blocks 80 or 90 percent of the sun's heat and glare. It also darkens the view a lot, so it suits doors in hard afternoon sun more than doors you look through all day.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: How do I tell what mesh my current screen is?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Count the openings. Cut a one-inch square in a piece of paper, hold it against the screen, and count the openings across and down. Eighteen across and sixteen down means 18 by 16 standard mesh.

sliding-screen-door-repair.q: How do lizards and bugs get in around a sliding screen door?
sliding-screen-door-repair.a: Through gaps. Check the bottom of the screen frame, the edge where it meets the glass door, and the pile weatherstrip along the sides. A screen that sits crooked on worn rollers leaves a gap at one corner.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: Why does my sliding closet door keep coming off the track?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: On mirror doors that roll on the floor, the door usually sits too low to stay captured in the top channel. On top-hung doors, look for a worn hanger wheel, a loose hanger screw, or a missing floor guide letting the bottom swing.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: How do I know if my closet door is top-hung or bottom-rolling?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: Slide one door aside and look at the floor. If the door's wheels sit in a floor track, it's bottom-rolling. If there's only a small guide block between the doors, the weight hangs from wheels in the top track.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: How do you get a mirrored closet door back on the track?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: With two people. Tip the bottom out, lift the top guides into the top channel, swing the bottom in, and lower the rollers into the floor track. Then raise the rollers until the door sits plumb and well up into the top track.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: Why is there a gap between my closet door and the wall?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: The door is out of plumb. Turn the adjusting screw on the roller or hanger nearest the wall to raise or lower that corner until the edge sits flush with the wall from top to bottom.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: What does the floor guide do on a bypass closet door?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: On top-hung doors, it keeps the two panels lined up and apart so they don't swing or rub. It doesn't carry any weight. If it's missing or broken, the doors swing at the bottom and can lever themselves off the track.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: What are anti-jump clips on closet doors?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: Small clips or tabs that stop a door from lifting out of its track. On many mirror doors, they snap into the track channel once the bottom roller is adjusted to the right height. Broken clips let the door pop out.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: Are mirrored closet doors safety glass?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: Most made today have a safety backing film on the mirror. They're backed to meet safety glazing standards. If yours cracks, leave the backing on, since it holds the broken glass together.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: Why are the edges of my mirror closet door turning black?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: That's desilvering, where moisture gets behind the mirror's coating. It can't be cleaned or adjusted away. Renin's warranty excludes black edges on doors installed within five miles of salt water, a distance that covers a lot of Florida homes.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: Can a closet door bottom track go on top of carpet?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: It's not recommended. Cut the carpet back and fasten the track to the floor, or set thin wood strips under the track. A track resting on pad flexes and lets the door drift.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: Which closet door goes in first, front or back?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: The back door goes in first, in the rear channel of the top and bottom tracks. The front door goes in the front channel after it. Reversing the order usually means taking both out again.

sliding-closet-door-repair.q: My bifold closet door drags on the floor. How do I raise it?
sliding-closet-door-repair.a: Adjust it at the pivot. Depending on the brand, the height adjustment is in the bottom pivot bracket or the top pivot. Lift the door slightly, turn the adjuster a little at a time, and check the gap at the floor.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Do I need a permit to replace a sliding glass door in Florida?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: Yes. The Florida Building Code requires a permit for replacing an exterior door, and door replacement isn't on its list of exempt work. Many counties offer a simpler replacement permit, but they still require product approval and an inspection.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: What is Florida Product Approval for doors?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: It's the state's approval showing a door model meets the Florida Building Code, identified by an FL number. You can look up any approved door in the state's database and see whether it's rated for the HVHZ, for impact, and to what design pressure.

A Notice of Acceptance is Miami-Dade County's product approval for building products that pass its testing. Doors installed in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, which covers Miami-Dade and Broward, need approval for HVHZ use, and an NOA is one way products show it.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Which Florida counties are in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: Broward and Miami-Dade. The Florida Building Code defines the HVHZ as those two counties, and products used there must be approved for HVHZ conditions. The rest of the state has its own wind requirements, which vary by location.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Do I have to install impact glass when I replace a sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: Not necessarily. Where the code requires opening protection, you can meet it with impact-rated glass or with approved shutters or panels. Your permit office decides what applies at your address, including any exceptions for older homes.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Are impact sliding doors worth it compared with shutters?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: It depends on how you live. Impact doors protect the opening all the time with nothing to put up, but they cost more and are much heavier. Shutters cost less and work only when they're installed before the storm.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: What does XO or OXXO mean on a sliding door quote?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: The letters describe the panels, read from outside the house. X is a panel that slides and O is a fixed panel. XO is a two-panel door with the left panel sliding, and OXXO is four panels with the two center ones sliding.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Who can legally replace a sliding glass door in Florida?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: A contractor licensed for it, such as a certified window and door installation specialty contractor, a glass and glazing contractor, or a general, building or residential contractor. Check any license with the state licensing board before you sign.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Can I get an insurance discount for impact sliding doors?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: Possibly. Florida law requires insurers to offer windstorm mitigation discounts that include opening protection, documented on a uniform mitigation verification form. Ask your insurance agent how a new door would affect your policy before you buy.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Is there still a federal tax credit for energy-efficient doors?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: Not for doors installed now. The federal energy-efficient home improvement credit doesn't apply to property placed in service after December 31, 2025. Check with a tax professional about your specific situation.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: Does my condo association have to approve a new sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: Often, yes. Many associations set rules for frame color, glass tint, impact rating and which contractors may work in the building. Get the association's written approval and requirements before ordering a made-to-size door.

sliding-glass-door-replacement.q: What should I look for on the energy rating label of a new sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-replacement.a: The U-factor and the Solar Heat Gain Coefficient. In Florida, a low SHGC usually matters most because it limits how much afternoon sun heats the room. Low-E glass coatings are what bring that number down.

patio-door-repair.q: What kind of patio door do I have?
patio-door-repair.a: Watch how it opens. Panels that slide on a bottom track are a slider. Panels that stack behind each other or vanish into the wall are a multi-slide. Panels on side hinges are a French or swinging door.

patio-door-repair.q: Why is my French patio door rubbing at the top?
patio-door-repair.a: It has sagged on its hinges, so the top corner on the latch side drops into the frame. Adjustable hinges have screws you turn a quarter turn at a time. Standard hinges are corrected with thin shims behind the hinge plate.

patio-door-repair.q: Why won't my French door latch without pushing hard?
patio-door-repair.a: The latch or the hooks of its multipoint lock are missing the strike plate, usually because the door has sagged. Fix the sag first, then loosen the strike screws and slide the strike to meet the latch, with a shim behind it if needed.

patio-door-repair.q: How do you adjust the panels on a multi-slide door?
patio-door-repair.a: One panel at a time. Each has its own rollers with a height adjuster, often a hex screw under a cover near the bottom. Take the weight off with a block, adjust, and check that the gap along the frame and the next panel is even.

patio-door-repair.q: Why do the middle panels of my four-panel slider not meet?
patio-door-repair.a: One center panel has dropped more than the other, so the edges where they lock together don't line up. Both panels need leveling to each other, not just to the frame, and worn rollers on either one need replacing.

patio-door-repair.q: Why does my multi-slide door leak at the sill?
patio-door-repair.a: Start with the weep holes, since a wide multi-slide sill drains several tracks. If it still leaks with clean weeps, the sill pan or installation underneath may be the problem, which needs someone to inspect it on site.

patio-door-repair.q: What is the passive panel on a French door?
patio-door-repair.a: It's the panel without the main handle, held closed by bolts that shoot into the head of the frame and the sill. The active panel latches against it. When the doors sag, those bolts often stop reaching their holes.

patio-door-repair.q: Do French doors need safety glass?
patio-door-repair.a: Glass in doors falls under federal safety glazing rules. Glass in a door other than a slider moves to the stricter Category II once any single piece is over 9 square feet, which large French door lites can reach.

patio-door-repair.q: How do I keep sand out of a multipoint lock?
patio-door-repair.a: Blow the mechanism out with compressed air, then lubricate it with a waterproof lubricant, the right choice near the coast. A lock that grinds or needs force to turn usually has grit in it.

patio-door-repair.q: Can a patio door be repaired if the brand is out of business?
patio-door-repair.a: Often, yes. Rollers, handles and weatherstrip can usually be matched by measuring the old parts. The harder cases are custom lock bodies and special extrusions, where a near match may need some fitting or a different approach.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.q: Who pays to fix a sliding door in a Miami condo, me or the association?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.a: Your declaration of condominium decides that, not a general rule. Look for the section on doors, windows and hurricane protection, or ask management in writing. Florida law also says an owner doesn't pay removal and reinstallation costs when the association's own repairs require them, unless the declaration says otherwise.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.q: Will the milestone inspection make me replace my sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.a: Not by itself. Florida's milestone inspection is a structural inspection of the building's load-bearing parts, and the statute doesn't mention doors. Miami-Dade's 30-year recertification report does record each exterior door's anchorage, latches and sealant, so a door in poor shape can end up in that report.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.q: Can I apply for a City of Miami door permit online?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.a: Yes. The City of Miami Building Department runs iBuild, an online portal where you can apply for a new permit, manage existing ones or make changes. Swapping rollers or a lock is normally a minor repair. Replacing the whole door is the job that needs the permit.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.q: How often should I clean the track on a slider facing Biscayne Bay?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.a: Monthly is a sensible schedule. Plan on hardware maintenance at least twice a year and monthly in coastal areas. Vacuum the sill, brush out the weep holes and check the rollers for rust or orange streaks along the track.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.q: Should I tell building management before a sliding door repair?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami.a: Yes, call them first. Ask what the building needs from a contractor, such as proof of insurance or a booked service elevator, and whether work hours are limited. Every building sets its own rules, so sort it out before the appointment rather than on the day.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.q: How do I find out who made my old sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.a: Look for a name etched into a corner of the glass or a label on the edge of the frame. With a brand and model, the parts search is quick. Without one, the door gets identified by measuring the roller, the handle's screw spacing and the panel, not by matching looks.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.q: Does the 25% rule apply to my Hialeah house?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.a: It may, if your home is a one- or two-family house built under codes in force before September 1, 1994. In the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, those homes can replace up to 25% of their glass area within 12 months without impact protection. Hialeah's building department makes the call.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.q: Who issues door replacement permits in Hialeah?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.a: The City of Hialeah's own building department, not Miami-Dade County. Because Hialeah is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, the new door needs an approval for HVHZ use, usually a Miami-Dade NOA. Ask the department what it needs before the door is ordered.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.q: Do sliding doors last longer inland than near the beach?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.a: Inland doors generally need less frequent maintenance, in our founder's experience, because salt is what speeds up corrosion on rollers and tracks. Heat and sun still take a toll. Plastic wheels, guides and handle pieces break down over the years, especially on a west-facing slider.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.q: Are nylon rollers OK for a house away from the coast?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hialeah.a: Usually, yes. Away from salt water, a good nylon or steel roller is normally fine, and stainless mostly earns its higher price near the coast. Whatever the material, match the new roller to the old one by measurement, because two rollers that look alike can differ in the housing or wheel.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.q: What does Miami Gardens ask for with a door replacement permit?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.a: The city's checklist lists a permit application, a homeowners association affidavit, an inspection procedure form, a floor plan, a uniform window and door schedule, a wind load chart and product approvals. A recorded notice of commencement is needed before the first inspection when the job is worth over $5,000.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.q: Do I have to be home for the door inspection in Miami Gardens?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.a: Yes, or send someone in your place. The city's inspection procedure form says the homeowner or a representative and the contractor or installer must both be present. The permit card, drawings and product approvals also have to be on site.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.q: Why does Miami Gardens want the trim left off for the inspection?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.a: So the inspector can see how the door is fastened. The attachment and final inspections happen together, and the city's form allows no trim, casings or interior caulking at that point, so shims and their spacing can be checked. Exterior caulking is allowed to keep the opening watertight.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.q: Can I show the door inspector photos on my phone?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.a: No. Miami Gardens' inspection procedure form says photos on a phone or other device aren't accepted. Where the inspector allows photos after the structural inspection, they have to be printed and labeled by opening number to match the window and door schedule.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.q: What should I add to an old slider that only has a latch?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miami-gardens.a: Add a second layer that works even if the latch is beaten. Miami-Dade County's home security checklist points to auxiliary locks or pins, and screws in the track so the panel can't be lifted out. A bar or blocker in the bottom track is the simplest place to start.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.q: Why does Miramar make me sign an HOA affidavit if I'm not in an HOA?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.a: Because the city code requires it from every applicant. Under City Code section 22-29(c)(1), you confirm you understand an association may add rules despite a city permit. If your home isn't in one, you initial the statement saying so and the affidavit is still filed.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.q: Does Miramar accept a Florida product approval or only a Miami-Dade NOA?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.a: Either one. Miramar's windows and doors package asks for a current Florida product approval or a Miami-Dade NOA for each new door, with the options circled that match your wind pressures and opening sizes. Because Broward is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, the approval has to cover HVHZ use.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.q: Do impact sliding doors need special rollers?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.a: They need rollers rated for the panel's weight. The industry roller standard tests roller assemblies at the load their maker rates them for. A light-duty roller under a laminated impact panel wears out early, so match the rating as well as the size.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.q: Can I pull my own door permit in Miramar instead of the contractor?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.a: Only if you aren't hiring one. Miramar's windows and doors package says that if a contractor is hired, the contractor must pull the permit. Owner-builder permits are for residential work only and need photo ID matching the job address, proof of ownership and confirmation of the homestead exemption.

sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.q: Which wind load chart does Miramar want with a door permit?
sliding-glass-door-repair-miramar.a: The Broward County Fenestration Wind Load Chart, marked for your building's height. Signed and sealed engineering wind load calculations can be used instead. For buildings 30 feet or taller, Broward's rules call for a site-specific design from a Florida engineer or architect.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.q: Can I still get parts for a 1990s sliding door in Pembroke Pines?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.a: Usually, but it can take some digging. Older impact models and doors from brands that stopped making parts are the hardest. We identify the model where we can and match rollers and handles by measurement, not by how they look in a photo.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.q: How old is the typical sliding door in a Pembroke Pines house?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.a: If it's original, about 30 years. The median Pembroke Pines home was built in 1992, and 37.6% of homes date from the 1990s. Many doors have been replaced since, so check for a date or label on the glass.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.q: Do I need HOA approval to change my screen mesh color in Pembroke Pines?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.a: Check your association's rules first. The city's building department tells owners in HOA communities to research the rules, covenants and deed restrictions and get approval before a project. A darker or solar mesh is the kind of visible change associations look at.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.q: Does Pembroke Pines ask for energy calculations on a replacement slider?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.a: Yes. The city's windows and doors permit checklist lists energy calculations along with product approvals, design wind pressures, the Broward County retrofit schedule and an inspection procedure form. The checklist notes it's subject to updates, so confirm the current version with the building department.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.q: What should I measure before ordering a roller for my Pembroke Pines slider?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pembroke-pines.a: Measure the old roller once it's out, not the door. Wheel diameter, housing length, width and height, and the position of the adjustment screw all matter. Two rollers that look alike online can differ by a few millimeters and ride badly in your track.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.q: Why does my Hollywood slider leak only when rain blows sideways?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.a: Wind pushes water into the sill faster than the weep holes can drain it. After Hurricane Ian, inspectors found that wind-driven rain entered homes mainly through sliding doors and soffits. Clear the weep holes and check the track for pitting or a bent lip.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.q: Does a house in a Hollywood historic district need approval for a new sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.a: It may. Hollywood has historic districts, including the Lakes Area district and the Hollywood Beach Historic Overlay District, and a Historic Preservation Board that rules on Certificates of Appropriateness. Ask the city's planning staff before ordering a door that changes how the house looks.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.q: Why do sliders near Hollywood Beach need more upkeep than ones further inland?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.a: Salt. It settles in the sill track, stays damp after rain and speeds up corrosion on rollers, screws and lock parts. Our founder's experience is that homes near the ocean need maintenance more often than inland homes, so clean the track more often.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.q: Can a 1960s sliding door in Hollywood still be repaired?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.a: Often, if the frame and bottom rail are sound. New rollers, a track cap and lock work can keep an old aluminum door going. The limit is parts: if the model can't be identified or its rollers aren't made anymore, replacement may be the honest answer.

sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.q: Who has to approve a new balcony slider in a Hollywood condo building?
sliding-glass-door-repair-hollywood.a: Usually two parties: the association or building management, and the city through a building permit. Broward is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so the door also needs a product approval that covers that zone. Get the association's requirements in writing before ordering.

sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.q: Do king tides affect sliding glass doors in Fort Lauderdale?
sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.a: Only if salt water reaches the door. The city says its highest tides typically come in September, October and November, and low streets and yards can flood. If tide water got onto your patio, rinse the track with fresh water that week so salt doesn't sit under the rollers.

sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.q: Can a Fort Lauderdale condo owner skip the door permit under the new HB 803 exemption?
sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.a: No. The city's HB 803 guide lists condominium, multifamily and apartment properties as not exempt, along with window replacements and properties in a flood hazard area. The exemption took effect July 1, 2026 and needs written approval even where it applies.

sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.q: Why do the rollers on my canal-front slider rust when the door never gets rained on?
sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.a: Salt air is enough. It settles in the sill and draws moisture, and a steel roller in an aluminum panel corrodes faster with salt around it. That's why we lean toward stainless rollers on doors within sight of the water, when the right size exists.

sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.q: When is the best time of year to service a slider in Fort Lauderdale?
sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.a: April or May, before hurricane season starts on June 1. Test the lock, check that the panel closes flush and clear the weep holes. On a waterfront door, a quick track cleaning every month and a closer look every three months keep salt from building up.

sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.q: Can a salt-stiffened lock on a Fort Lauderdale slider be cleaned instead of replaced?
sliding-glass-door-repair-fort-lauderdal.a: Often, if the corrosion is on the outside. Cleaning, a lubricant the door maker approves and an adjustment can bring a stiff latch back. If the lock body is corroded inside or the latch hook is pitted, replacing the lock is the fix that lasts.

sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.q: How do I identify the sliding door on my Davie manufactured home?
sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.a: Look for its certification label. Federal rules require sliding glass doors in manufactured homes to be certified to a recognized door standard and to carry a label from a certification body. Photograph it and send it with your request.

sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.q: My Davie pool was approved with door alarms. What happens if I replace the slider?
sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.a: Plan to put the alarm back on the new door. Exit alarms are one of the pool safety options under Florida law, rated at least 85 dB A at 10 feet. Ask the town's building division what it expects for your home before the old door comes out.

sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.q: Why does my Davie slider grind when we live nowhere near the beach?
sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.a: Grit. Dirt, sand and debris from yards and pool decks collect in the track, mix with old grease and wear down the rollers. Vacuum the track first. If it still grinds with a clean track, the rollers are worn or the rail is scored.

sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.q: Does a new sliding door in Davie need Miami-Dade approval?
sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.a: It needs an approval that covers the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, because Davie is in Broward County. That's usually a Miami-Dade NOA or a Florida product approval marked for HVHZ use. The building division confirms what it accepts with the permit.

sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.q: Can a manufactured home slider use the same rollers as a house slider?
sliding-glass-door-repair-davie.a: Not necessarily. Doors built for manufactured homes can differ in panel weight, housing size and track profile from site-built doors. We match the roller to the old one by measurement, since a part that looks right can still sit at the wrong height.

sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.q: Who can pull a door replacement permit in Plantation?
sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.a: A licensed contractor registered with the City of Plantation, or the homeowner as an owner-builder. The city says owner-builders must meet with the plan reviewer before applying for any permit, and the product needs Miami-Dade or Florida approval.

sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.q: Does a Plantation building permit mean my HOA has approved the new door?
sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.a: No. The city states that issuing a building permit doesn't mean the work is approved by a condo, homeowners or property owners association. Get the association's approval separately, ideally in writing, before ordering a replacement door.

sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.q: Does the year my Plantation house was built matter for a new door?
sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.a: Yes, it can. Broward is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, and the Florida Building Code lets one- and two-family homes built under codes before September 1, 1994 replace up to 25% of their glazed openings in 12 months without impact protection. The building department confirms.

sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.q: Can you find rollers for an old aluminum slider with no brand label?
sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.a: Often, yes. We measure the old roller's wheel, housing and mounting and match it to what's still made. Some discontinued doors have no compatible part left, and when that leaves the panel unable to roll properly, replacement becomes the honest answer.

sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.q: Do leaves from shade trees really affect a sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-repair-plantation.a: Yes. Leaves, seed pods and grit collect in the sill track and clog the weep holes that drain it. Water then sits in the track and the rollers grind through debris. Vacuuming the track and brushing out the drain slots regularly helps.

sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.q: Can I get a door permit at the Sunrise Building Division without an appointment?
sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.a: Usually, yes. The Building Division lists windows, doors and shutters among the structural items accepted at walk-through permitting on Tuesday and Thursday mornings from 8:00 to 10:00 AM. Call (954) 572-2354 first, since walk-in hours can change.

sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.q: My condo board has hurricane protection specs. Does a new slider have to follow them?
sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.a: Plan on it. Florida law requires condo boards to adopt hurricane protection specifications that comply with the building code. Where approval is required, the board can't refuse an owner's hurricane protection that conforms to those specifications, so get a copy before choosing a door.

sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.q: Can a sliding door be made easier to open for an older parent?
sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.a: In most cases, yes. A heavy door usually has worn rollers or a dirty track, and new rollers with a cleaned, adjusted track can bring it back to a one-hand push. A handle with an easier lever may also fit the existing holes.

sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.q: Can the closet doors and the balcony slider be fixed in the same visit?
sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.a: Yes, tell us about both when you call. Mirrored closet doors use different, smaller rollers and guides than a patio slider, so a photo of each door helps us bring parts that fit both.

sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.q: What should I photograph before calling about a condo slider in Sunrise?
sliding-glass-door-repair-sunrise.a: Take a photo of the whole door, the label etched in a glass corner or on the frame edge, the handle, and the bottom of the panel where it meets the track. Those four pictures usually show the brand, the hardware and where it's failing.

sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.q: What does Coral Springs want to see for a sliding door replacement permit?
sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.a: The city's retrofit checklist asks for the job value, a site plan showing each replaced opening, product approvals with the city's submittal form, and wind load paperwork with the Broward County Uniform Retrofit Window & Door Schedule. Condos also get zoning and fire review.

sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.q: Can I paint my sliding door frame any color in Coral Springs?
sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.a: Not necessarily. The city lets residents paint the front door, garage door and trim (under 10% of the house) any color, but a slider frame isn't named. Check with Community Development and with your HOA before painting it something bold.

sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.q: Is a Notice of Commencement needed for a door replacement in Coral Springs?
sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.a: Only if the job is over $5,000. The city's windows and doors retrofit checklist says the recorded notice is required before the first inspection when the job value passes that amount.

sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.q: Do I still need shutters if my new slider has impact glass?
sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.a: Usually not. The Coral Springs retrofit checklist says shutters aren't required for impact-resistant windows, and impact-rated glazing is one way to meet the hurricane protection rules. Confirm with the building department for your specific door and product approval.

sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.q: Can kids break a sliding glass door by running into it?
sliding-glass-door-repair-coral-springs.a: It can happen, which is why federal rules require sliding door glass to pass a high-impact safety test, in practice tempered or laminated glass. Tempered glass breaks into small pieces instead of sharp shards. Replace any cracked panel quickly.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.q: Does Pompano Beach make me pull a permit just to swap the rollers?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.a: No, as a rule. The city's window and door checklist says a permit isn't required to replace a part that doesn't alter the door's approval or make it unsafe. Installing a new door or doing a major repair does need a building permit.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.q: Does a door replacement in Pompano Beach qualify for the under-$7,500 permit exemption?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.a: No. The city's notice on House Bill 803 says installing or replacing exterior windows and doors is structural work, so it always needs a standard building permit, whatever the price.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.q: What does an oceanfront condo need for a new slider permit in Pompano Beach?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.a: An association approval letter is on the city's checklist, along with a product approval and a wind load chart. If the building's mean roof height is over 30 feet, the city also wants site-specific wind loads signed and sealed by a design professional.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.q: Why do the rollers on my aluminum balcony door rust?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.a: Because many rollers have steel bearings or axles, and they sit inside an aluminum panel. With salt water between two different metals, one corrodes. Stainless steel rollers hold up better near the ocean, if one is made in your door's size.

sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.q: Can I replace my own condo slider in Pompano Beach as an owner-builder?
sliding-glass-door-repair-pompano-beach.a: No. The city's window, door and shutter checklist says the owner-builder option doesn't apply to work in condominiums, so a licensed contractor has to pull the permit for a condo door replacement.

sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.q: Why does my Deerfield Beach slider take two hands to open?
sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.a: Worn rollers or a dirty track, most of the time. When the wheels in the bottom rail wear flat or their bearings seize, they skid instead of rolling. Near the beach, salt corrodes steel bearings faster. Inland, years of dirt in the track do the same kind of damage more slowly.

sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.q: Is a new sliding door in Deerfield Beach held to HVHZ rules?
sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.a: Yes. Broward County is in the Florida Building Code's High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so a replacement door needs a product approval that covers HVHZ use, usually a Miami-Dade NOA or a Florida approval marked for HVHZ. Repairs to rollers, tracks and locks don't change the door's approval.

sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.q: What is the Broward Uniform Retrofit Window & Door Schedule?
sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.a: It's the shared form Broward's Board of Rules and Appeals requires for window and door replacement permits across the county. Each opening gets a line with its size, product approval, design pressure and glass type. Your contractor fills it out as part of the permit application for a new door.

sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.q: Can my Deerfield Beach condo board reject the impact door I picked?
sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.a: Not if it meets the board's adopted specifications. Under Florida condo law, a board can't refuse hurricane protection that conforms to its specifications, but it can require the door to match the building's existing outside appearance. Get the specifications before you order.

sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.q: Does the Deerfield Beach Community Appearance Board review door changes?
sliding-glass-door-repair-deerfield-beac.a: It can, for some buildings. The board reviews the exterior look of multi-family, commercial and industrial properties in the city. A repair that doesn't change how the door looks isn't an appearance change. For a new door in a different style or color, ask the city's planning staff first.

sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.q: Why are door rules stricter in Deerfield Beach than in Boca Raton?
sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.a: Because the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone stops at the county line. The Florida Building Code applies it only to Broward and Miami-Dade, so a new door in Deerfield Beach needs an HVHZ approval. In Boca Raton, a Florida product approval for use outside the HVHZ is the normal route.

sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.q: Is Boca Raton in a wind-borne debris region?
sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.a: Expect it to be. All of unincorporated Palm Beach County is in the wind-borne debris region, where glazed openings need impact glass or approved protection. The city's building division confirms the requirement for your address when you apply for a permit.

sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.q: What paperwork has to be at the house for a Boca Raton door inspection?
sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.a: The product approval or Miami-Dade NOA for every door being installed. The city's over-the-counter affidavit says missing approvals can fail the inspection and bring re-inspection fees. Each installed door also needs its own scheduled inspection.

sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.q: Can one panel of a multi-slide door be fixed without touching the rest?
sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.a: Often, yes. Each moving panel on a multi-slide door rides on its own rollers with its own height adjustment, so one sagging panel can be lifted, adjusted or given new rollers alone. If the interlock where panels meet has shifted, the neighboring panel may need a small adjustment too.

sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.q: Why does Boca Raton ask for water testing on some new doors?
sliding-glass-door-repair-boca-raton.a: Because the building code requires it for doors that don't meet certain exceptions. The city's window and door schedule says doors not meeting exceptions 1 and 2 of Florida Building Code sections 1709.5.1 and R609.3 must be tested for water infiltration. The door's product documents show which applies.

sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.q: Do I need a certificate of appropriateness to replace a sliding door in a West Palm Beach historic district?
sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.a: Yes, when the new door changes the exterior. The city's 2023 application lists a change in door material or style as a staff-level review. A new or resized opening on the main facade goes to the Historic Preservation Board, while one on a side or rear facade stays with staff.

sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.q: Does fixing rollers on a historic house in West Palm Beach need historic review?
sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.a: Not as a rule. The city's certificate of appropriateness covers work that changes a building's exterior appearance, and new rollers or a lock inside the frame don't. If the repair turns into a new door or a different visible handle style, check with the city's historic staff first.

sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.q: Can I put a vinyl sliding door on a historic home in West Palm Beach?
sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.a: Ask the city before you buy one. Its guidance says vinyl is generally not permitted for windows on historic properties and points to aluminum impact products for in-kind replacement. It doesn't spell out sliding doors, so historic staff decides.

sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.q: Which West Palm Beach neighborhoods are historic districts?
sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.a: The city has 18 locally designated districts. Its historic district map names areas such as Old Northwood, Northwood Hills, El Cid, Flamingo Park, Grandview Heights, Prospect/Southland Park and Mango Promenade. The city's Historic Property Search map shows whether a specific house is designated.

sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.q: What does West Palm Beach check on a replacement sliding door?
sliding-glass-door-repair-west-palm-beac.a: Wind loads and product approval. Replacing a door needs a permit, the product must meet the wind loads in West Palm Beach, and it must be installed according to the manufacturer's product approval documents. Palm Beach County is outside the HVHZ, so no HVHZ approval is needed.
